title: Cover WebView status and rename readiness guardrails
summary: Record ownership for existing WebView diagnostics status presentation, diagnostics handoff status, queue mutation-boundary copy, rename apply readiness, and rename apply outcome guardrail edits.
reason: Strict change-control coverage identified coherent WebView edits without packet ownership. The edits keep diagnostics status state visible, show diagnostics handoff destination state, clarify that queue staging controls are not launch scope, make rename apply scope require checked rows before backend mutation, and expose rename apply outcome counts for skipped/protected/failed rows.
behavior_before: Diagnostics status text did not consistently expose panel state, diagnostics handoff destination state was only implicit, queue summary guardrails did not distinguish local staging controls from launch scope, and rename apply readiness/outcome copy could describe fallback behavior or result counts less strictly than the checked-row-only guardrail.
behavior_after: Diagnostics status surfaces panel state where available, diagnostics handoff writes destination status locally, active job and log summaries expose ready/warning/blocked/empty state, queue summaries clarify backend-owned launch/mutation boundaries, rename apply readiness requires checked rows with duplicate/readiness evidence before backend apply, and apply outcome counts include skipped/protected/failed row evidence.
manual_validation: git diff inspected for the uncovered WebView diagnostics, rename, queue-adjacent status, and diagnostics browser smoke files; source code left unchanged during packet creation except packet metadata
rollback_plan: Remove this packet, its generated summary, and revert the WebView diagnostics, queue summary, and rename status/readiness edits only if the owning WebView change is intentionally backed out.
notes: Coverage packet only for existing WebView source edits. It must not add frontend filesystem mutation, bypass backend rename.apply ownership, or change media policy.
